#### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

USH 18 will remain open to traffic throughout the project. Lane closures can be maintained 24 hours a day, except during the lane closure restriction times or holidays and events where the roadway must be opened back up. This will be necessary to limit the amount of Special High Early Strength (SHES) concrete used on the project. SHES concrete has a much higher price and lower overall service life. All lane and ramp closures are subject to the approval of the Region traffic engineer. When the work zone is not active the traffic control drums must be placed completely within the closed lane to accommodate OSOW vehicles. Access to all businesses along and near the USH 18 corridor will be maintain. There are no schools directly within the project limits. Schools near the project area are located within the Village of Mount Horeb. No impacts to schools are anticipated. Northbound STH 78 will be detoured down to the USH 18/USH 151/CTH ID interchange while work along STH 78 is completed. Southbound STH 78 will remain open at all times. CTH ID interchange will require a detour for the two EB ramps for a structure closure on the bridge work. A detour will be posted to allow for the work on the structure to allow them to complete before the ironman Wisconsin(Sept 11). Northbound CTH ID will be detoured down to the USH 18/USH 151/CTH PD interchange while work along CTH ID is completed. Southbound CTH ID will be detoured down to USH 18/USH 151/STH 78 interchange while work on structure takes place. CTH JG will be closed while the wing wall, bearings and north abutment expansion joint are replaced at B-13-300 (CTH JG over USH 18). Interim liquidated damages will be accessed if the STH 78 and CTH ID detours or the CTH JG closure exceeds the maximum calendars days shown in the special provisions. The STH 78 and CTH ID detours will not be allowed to occur at the same time. Closure of CTH JG is not permitted while the STH 78 or CTH ID detours are in place. No impacts to businesses, schools, and everyday services are anticipated while these detours or closure are in place.

#### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Currently there are no ADA facilities or pedestrian facilities present within the project limits; however, the Military Ridge State Trail parallels USH 18 from STH 78 to just west of Erbe Road. While there are no direct impacts to the Military Ridge State Trail, there will be work along Erbe Road and STH 78 where the Military Ridge State Trail crosses each roadway. Access to and crossings of the Military Ridge State Trail will be maintain at all times. #### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

Access to traffic generators will be maintained throughout construction. The milling and paving operations along mainline STH 172 will be completed under traffic. Single lane closures will be permitted in both directions. A full closure will be required to complete the work along the single lane STH 172/IH 41 interchange ramps. Traffic will be detoured for the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 while the concrete pavement is being replaced. The detour will direct traffic along NB IH 41 to CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue). The work for the other single lane ramps will not have detours but lane closures will be allowed as specified in the lane closures.

#### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

The curb ramps at the STH 172 & Packerland Drive/CTH EB and the STH 172 & Babcock Road intersections will be replaced with the project. While the curb ramps are being replaced the associated Packerland Drive bike trail will be closed and appropriate signage will be in place (see attached Traffic Control Plan). The public will be informed of the planned work and closure of the path through public involvement meetings, press releases/media alerts, the project website, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website.

#### **Describe how impacts to airports will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Airport personnel will be notified of the project and will be kept informed of changes in traffic control during construction by construction personnel. Lane closures will only be allowed during the times specified in the special provisions. The public will be informed of the planned work and lane closures through public involvement meetings, press releases/media alerts, the project website, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

IH 41 and CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue) traffic will be impacted by the project. Traffic along the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 will be detoured along NB IH 41 to CTH VK while the concrete pavement along the ramp is being replaced. The detour route will be signed per the traffic control plans.

#### **Does the project affect other regions/states?**

No.

#### **How will traffic disruptions be minimized during listed events and holidays?**

The special provisions will include language indicating, "Do not perform work on, nor haul materials of any kind along or across any portion of the highway carrying STH 172 traffic and entirely clear the traveled way and shoulders of such portions of the highway of equipment, barricades, signs, lights, and any other material that might impede the free flow of traffic during the events listed above".
